subproblem.title: Orthogonal projection onto a 2-plane in an orthonormal frame
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2, and a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0. Then for every x ∈ ℝ^P the orthogonal projection of x onto Q is Q.starProjection x = ⟨x, a⟩a + ⟨x, e⟩e.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → ∀ x : Euclid P, Q.starProjection x = inner ℝ x a • a + inner ℝ x e • e
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (F1) of the supplied localization proof, isolated as the frame formula. Notation: π := Q.starProjection. ⟨·,·⟩ is the real Euclidean inner product, so it is symmetric (⟨u, w⟩ = ⟨w, u⟩, real_inner_comm). |·| is the Euclidean norm.
1. (Orthonormality.) The two-element family (a, e), written ![a, e] in Lean, is orthonormal: ⟨a, a⟩ = |a|² = 1, ⟨e, e⟩ = |e|² = 1, and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0 = ⟨e, a⟩ by hypothesis and symmetry (orthonormal_iff_ite). So it is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent).
2. (span{a, e} = Q.) Since a ∈ Q and e ∈ Q, span{a, e} ≤ Q (Submodule.span_le). A linearly independent family of two vectors spans a subspace of dimension 2 (finrank_span_eq_card), and Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 by hypothesis; Q is finite-dimensional, being a subspace of ℝ^P. A subspace contained in a finite-dimensional subspace of the same dimension equals it (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq). So span{a, e} = Q.
3. (Candidate.) Put y := ⟨x, a⟩a + ⟨x, e⟩e. Since a, e ∈ Q and Q is a linear subspace, y ∈ Q.
4. (Orthogonality.) Let w ∈ Q. By step 2, w ∈ span{a, e}, so w = c₀a + c₁e for some reals c₀, c₁ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). Using bilinearity, |a|² = |e|² = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = ⟨e, a⟩ = 0:
⟨x − y, a⟩ = ⟨x, a⟩ − ⟨x, a⟩⟨a, a⟩ − ⟨x, e⟩⟨e, a⟩ = 0,
⟨x − y, e⟩ = ⟨x, e⟩ − ⟨x, a⟩⟨a, e⟩ − ⟨x, e⟩⟨e, e⟩ = 0.
Hence ⟨x − y, w⟩ = c₀⟨x − y, a⟩ + c₁⟨x − y, e⟩ = 0.
5. (Characterization of π.) Q is finite-dimensional, hence complete, so it has an orthogonal projection. The projection of x is the unique point of Q whose difference from x is orthogonal to Q: if y ∈ Q and ⟨x − y, w⟩ = 0 for every w ∈ Q, then πx = y (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). By steps 3 and 4, Q.starProjection x = ⟨x, a⟩a + ⟨x, e⟩e. ∎
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is orthonormal, hence linearly independent; span{a, e} ≤ Q and both have finrank 2, so span{a, e} = Q (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).
y := ⟨x,a⟩a + ⟨x,e⟩e lies in Q, and ⟨x − y, a⟩ = ⟨x − y, e⟩ = 0, so ⟨x − y, w⟩ = 0 for every w = c₀a + c₁e ∈ Q.

Each proof step is valid: orthonormality gives independence, the dimension comparison gives span{a,e}=Q, and the candidate lies in Q with orthogonal residual. Projection uniqueness proves the exact conclusion without circular dependence. This is a genuine linear-algebra obligation.

subproblem.title: Polar distance bound: |x − a| ≤ ||x| − 1| + |angle| + η + η²
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, and π := Q.starProjection (the orthogonal projection onto Q). Then for every x ∈ ℝ^P with ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, writing η := |x − πx|/|x|, we have |x − a| ≤ ||x| − 1| + |arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩)| + η + η².
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → ∀ x : Euclid P, 0 < inner ℝ x a → dist x a ≤ |‖x‖ - 1| + |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| + ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ / ‖x‖ + (‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ / ‖x‖) ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4–7 of the supplied localization proof (normalization, direction of πx̂, the three estimates and the triangle inequality), for an arbitrary x with ⟨x, a⟩ > 0. The bound is kept in the form η + η². The simplification η² ≤ η/2, which needs η ≤ 1/2, stays in the parent. Notation: π := Q.starProjection, q(x) := x − πx, r := |x|, α := ⟨x, a⟩, β := ⟨x, e⟩, f := arctan(β/α), η := |q(x)|/r, and dist x a = |x − a|. ⟨·,·⟩ is real, so it is symmetric.
1. (Positivity.) Since α = ⟨x, a⟩ > 0 and ⟨0, a⟩ = 0, x ≠ 0. So r > 0 and η ≥ 0.
2. (Frame formula, from the sibling frame_projection.) Apply the sibling lemma Submission.idtp_cse_etp_loc_frame_projection to P, Q, a, e and x; its hypotheses are exactly ours. It gives πx = αa + βe. Let ρ := |πx|. Expanding ⟨αa + βe, αa + βe⟩ with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = ⟨e, a⟩ = 0 gives ρ² = α² + β². So ρ² ≥ α² > 0, hence ρ > 0.
3. (Pythagoras.) πx ∈ Q (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem) and ⟨x − πx, w⟩ = 0 for all w ∈ Q (Submodule.starProjection_inner_eq_zero), so ⟨πx, q(x)⟩ = 0. Since x = πx + q(x), norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero gives r² = ρ² + |q(x)|². So ρ² ≤ r², and since both are nonnegative, ρ ≤ r. Dividing by r² > 0 gives (ρ/r)² = 1 − η². Since 0 ≤ ρ/r ≤ 1, ρ/r ≥ (ρ/r)² = 1 − η².
4. (Angle.) By Real.cos_arctan, cos f = 1/√(1 + (β/α)²). Since α > 0, 1 + (β/α)² = (α² + β²)/α² = ρ²/α² = (ρ/α)·(ρ/α) with ρ/α > 0. So √(1 + (β/α)²) = ρ/α (Real.sqrt_eq_iff_mul_self_eq_of_pos), and cos f = α/ρ.
5. (Decomposition.) Since r⁻¹q(x) = r⁻¹x − r⁻¹πx, the right-hand side below telescopes as x − r⁻¹x + r⁻¹x − r⁻¹πx + r⁻¹πx − ρ⁻¹πx + ρ⁻¹πx − a = x − a. Hence
x − a = (1 − r⁻¹)x + r⁻¹q(x) + (r⁻¹ − ρ⁻¹)πx + (ρ⁻¹πx − a).
In the parent's notation, with x̂ := x/|x|, v := πx/|πx| = ρ⁻¹πx and π linear, these four terms are x − x̂, q(x̂), πx̂ − v and v − a.
6. (Four estimates.)
(a) Since r > 0, |(1 − r⁻¹)x| = |1 − r⁻¹|·r = |(r − 1)/r|·r = |r − 1|.
(b) |r⁻¹q(x)| = |q(x)|/r = η.
(c) Since 0 < ρ ≤ r, r⁻¹ ≤ ρ⁻¹. So |(r⁻¹ − ρ⁻¹)πx| = (ρ⁻¹ − r⁻¹)ρ = 1 − ρ/r ≤ 1 − (1 − η²) = η², by step 3.
(d) By step 2, ρ⁻¹πx − a = (α/ρ − 1)a + (β/ρ)e. So |ρ⁻¹πx − a|² = (α/ρ − 1)² + (β/ρ)² = (α² + β²)/ρ² − 2α/ρ + 1 = 2 − 2α/ρ = 2 − 2cos f, by steps 2 and 4. Since cos f ≥ 1 − f²/2 (Real.one_sub_sq_div_two_le_cos), |ρ⁻¹πx − a|² ≤ f² = |f|². Both |ρ⁻¹πx − a| and |f| are nonnegative, so |ρ⁻¹πx − a| ≤ |f| (pow_le_pow_iff_left₀).
7. (Triangle inequality.) Step 5, the triangle inequality and (a)–(d) give
dist x a = |x − a| ≤ |r − 1| + η + η² + |f| = ||x| − 1| + |arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩)| + |x − πx|/|x| + (|x − πx|/|x|)². ∎
proof_key_steps: Since ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, x ≠ 0 and r = |x| > 0. By frame_projection, πx = αa + βe, so ρ² := |πx|² = α² + β² > 0.
Pythagoras gives r² = ρ² + |q(x)|², so ρ ≤ r, (ρ/r)² = 1 − η², and 1 − ρ/r ≤ η².
Since α > 0, cos arctan(β/α) = α/ρ, so |ρ⁻¹πx − a|² = 2 − 2cos f ≤ f² (one_sub_sq_div_two_le_cos).
x − a = (1 − r⁻¹)x + r⁻¹q(x) + (r⁻¹ − ρ⁻¹)πx + (ρ⁻¹πx − a). The four norms are bounded by |r − 1|, η, η² and |f|, and the triangle inequality gives the bound.
